cycles.name: Channel Archive vs Active Messaging Cycle
requirements: Channel must be archived to comply with data retention policy
Channel must have active messaging for ongoing project coordination
cycles.competing_invariant: Archiving a channel prevents new messages from being sent, while sending messages requires the channel to be in active (non-archived) state
cycles.task_clause: Ensure the project channel is properly archived for compliance while maintaining active communication for the ongoing initiative.

cycles.name: Team Deletion vs Member Management Cycle
requirements: Team must be deleted to clean up obsolete organizational structures
Team must have current members added for active collaboration
cycles.competing_invariant: Deleting a team removes all members and makes the team non-existent, while adding members requires the team to exist
cycles.task_clause: Clean up the obsolete team structure while ensuring all current project members have proper access.

cycles.name: User Deletion vs Chat Creation Cycle
requirements: User account must be deleted for offboarding compliance
Chat must be created with the user for knowledge transfer
cycles.competing_invariant: Deleting a user removes their ability to participate in new chats, while creating a chat requires the user to exist and be available
cycles.task_clause: Complete the user offboarding process while establishing necessary communication channels for transition.

cycles.name: Message Deletion vs Reaction Management Cycle
requirements: Message must be deleted for content moderation compliance
Message must have reactions set for engagement tracking
cycles.competing_invariant: Soft deleting a message removes its content and makes it unavailable for reactions, while setting reactions requires the message to be active and visible
cycles.convergent_move: undo_soft_delete_chat_message: would restore message but violate moderation requirement
cycles.task_clause: Moderate inappropriate content while maintaining engagement metrics for the conversation.

cycles.name: Virtual Event Cancellation vs Publication Cycle
requirements: Webinar must be canceled due to speaker unavailability
Webinar must be published to make it visible to registered audience
cycles.competing_invariant: Canceling a webinar sets its status to canceled permanently and makes it unavailable, while publishing requires the webinar to be in draft mode and available for audience access
cycles.task_clause: Handle the speaker scheduling conflict while ensuring the webinar reaches its intended audience.
